items.label: Artificial Intelligence
items.notes: Catalog lists "CSE 150A or CSE 150B or CSE 151B" here and CSE 151B again as the Deep Learning core course; one course cannot fill both slots.

items.label: Ethics
items.notes: "Ethics: Four units". The catalog lists it under Core Courses, though its core total is twenty units (CSE 100, 101, AI, 151A, 151B).

items.label: AI Electives
items.notes: Twelve units of AI electives chosen from the list (which are not used to satisfy other core or breadth elective requirements).

items.label: Applications of Computing breadth
items.notes: Students may use up to eight units of ENG 100D/L courses toward upper-division CSE elective credits (as part of the twelve-unit maximum of special studies courses - CSE 197, 198, 199, 199H). Students may only take ENG 100D once.

items.text: Any CSE upper-division course between CSE 100-194 that is not being used for another major requirement, with the exception of CSE 180/180R and CSE 191 which are not allowed to meet CSE upper-division CSE elective requirements.
CSE upper-division or graduate courses or non-CSE classes that are tagged with one of the three tags (which are not used to satisfy the core or breadth elective requirements)

items.label: Additional electives
items.notes: Students may use twelve units of CSE 190 toward CSE elective credit (repeatable up to three times for different topics; CSE 291 applies to this twelve-unit maximum). Undergraduate students may petition to use graduate-level course work toward their elective requirements.

items.label: Electives
items.notes: 28 units of elective courses. Electives must give sufficient breadth within these outcomes (Systems, Theory/Abstraction, Applications of Computing). A maximum of twelve units of P/NP courses may count, chosen from: a maximum of eight units of CSE 198 or 199 or 199H; a maximum of four units of CSE 197; a maximum of two units of CSE 109.

requirement.notes: Students must complete sixty-four upper-division units: twenty units of core courses and forty-four units of elective courses.

narrative: All major requirements for each degree program must be completed with a C– or better, except for courses offered Pass/No Pass only.
All major requirements and upper-division electives except CSE 91, 95, 109, 197, 198, or 199 must be taken for a letter grade.
To graduate, a minimum grade point average of 2.0 will be required in upper-division courses in the major, including upper-division electives.
At most four units of CSE 197 may be used toward technical elective requirements.
CSE 195 cannot be used toward course requirements.
Students may not get duplicate credit for equivalent courses.

Selective major: admission for continuing students is by selective major application (screening courses: CSE 8B or 11, CSE 12, CSE 29 or ECE 15 or CSE 15L, CSE 20, CSE 21, CSE 30 or ECE 30, CSE 100 (R), and CSE 101 for applicants after second year).
The BS artificial intelligence program requires a total of 124 units (not including the general-education requirements).
Students are expected to complete the following sixty units [lower-division] by the end of their sophomore year.
Students must complete sixty-four upper-division units: twenty units of core courses and forty-four units of elective courses.
The page also lists 'Technical Electives for all CSE Majors'; the BS artificial intelligence elective rules themselves are stated in terms of the AI elective list and the program-level tags.
